trust_decision.summary: Whether a host is IDN-canonicalised before it is emitted is decided by the canonicalisation block inside parseWithStatus; resolve() disables that block by parsing both inputs with {scheme:'null'}, then composes a fresh host in resolveComponent and serialises it without re-running the check with the final resolved scheme.

landing_point.why: The advisory names scheme-relative references, whose only handling is in resolve(); at index.js:51 the host composed by resolveComponent is handed straight to serialize with no host check.

fix_sites.entry_point: fast-uri.parse (also reached by normalize, equal, resolve)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: index.js:63 (resolveComponent, exported at index.js:525 and typed at types/index.d.ts:41)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: resolveComponent() is a low-level component API that returns components rather than a URI string; canonicalisation belongs to the string-level resolve(), so a caller that composes components is responsible for its own host.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Percent-encoded ASCII hosts (e.g. //trusted.com%40evil.com/path) must keep resolving to an unchanged encoded host, not fail closed: WHATWG's hostname parser rejects them while fast-uri preserves them as RFC 3986 data, so a fix that throws on every failed conversion breaks an existing assertion.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: test/security.test.js:111-117 (assertion) and index.js:443-448 (unescape/reescape that produces such hosts)

O6_input_shapes: scheme-relative reference whose authority replaces the base host (//127。0。0。1/private)
path-relative reference that inherits the base host (base 'https://ex\u00ADample.com/base' + 'child')
absolute reference that supplies its own scheme (http://ex\u200Bample.com/)
host with an encoded dot that WHATWG cannot convert (//\u200D.example%2Etest/) - must throw
percent-encoded ASCII host (trusted.com%40evil.com) - must be preserved, not rejected
IPv4 / bracketed IPv6 literal composed host - conversion skipped
unsupported scheme (uri://) and options unicodeSupport:true - host preserved

O7_producer.where: index.js:63 (resolveComponent composes target.host from base/relative at index.js:76, index.js:83-85, index.js:113-114)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: serialize(component) emits component.host verbatim through recomposeAuthority; no IDN canonicalisation and no refusal for an unconvertible host.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: serialize consumes already-parsed component fields as trusted data and only re-escapes delimiters (test/security.test.js:119-125); canonicalising there would also break the documented unicodeSupport/IRI round-trip (README.md:30-34).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file (index.js), ~90 lines below the fix site; sink in lib/utils.js

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A reference with no scheme at all keeps its IDN host: normalize('//127。0。0。1/x'), parse('//host') and resolve('//ex\u00ADample.com/a','b') all skip the canonicalisation gate because no scheme handler is found and options.domainHost is unset.
O8_uncovered_routes.where: index.js:426-438 (gate at index.js:427 and index.js:429), reached from index.js:12-18 and index.js:478
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: with no scheme there is no domain-host context to decide with; the documented domainHost/scheme options exist precisely for callers who know the scheme (README.md:18-19, README.md:33-34), so the host is preserved.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function that already contains the check; no file distance

O8b_injection_room.sibling: canonicalise the composed host inside resolveComponent instead of in resolve
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: resolveComponent is the exported composition primitive that picks target.host; a maintainer hardening the sink would naturally move the check down to where the host is chosen.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: convert or refuse a non-ASCII reg-name in recomposeAuthority before emitting the authority
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: recomposeAuthority is the single funnel every host passes through on output, so it is the obvious place for a 'no raw Unicode host' guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: apply the domain-host check in serialize() when the resolved scheme/options request it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: serialize already resolves a scheme handler at index.js:167, so extending it to the host looks like a small, symmetric change.

O9_family: host confusion / URI interpretation conflict (CWE-436): skipped IDN-to-ASCII canonicalisation of a composed host creates a parser differential with WHATWG URL

O10_build.toolchain: npm; tape test runner; eslint/neostandard lint; tstyche for types (package.json:48-59)
O10_build.project_tests: test/security.test.js (host/authority hardening), test/resolve.test.js (RFC 3986 resolution examples), test/uri-js.test.js (IDN/domainHost), test/parse.test.js, test/serialize.test.js; run with npm run test:unit -> tape test/**/*.js (package.json:56).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Canonicalise only the relative reference's own host (for example inside parseWithStatus when the relative has an authority), which leaves a host inherited from the base and the final-scheme decision unhandled.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/schemes.js:397-432 (mailtoNormalizeDomain) is a separate domain-to-ASCII implementation in another file, but it serves the mailto recipient list under a handler that sets unicodeSupport:true, not the authority host; not pursued.
